issues.issue: What standard of review applies to the Agency's findings on the interchange and interswitching issues?
issues.applicant_position: Some issues, including extraterritorial application, should get correctness review; CN raised this only in oral argument.
issues.respondent_position: Reasonableness applies, as the parties agreed; the Agency gets a wide margin of appreciation.
issues.result_quote: This inquiry is whether the Agency’s findings are unreasonable.

issues.issue: Was it unreasonable for the Agency to find that BNSF's rights under the 1912 Agreement gave it a line of railway in Canada?
issues.applicant_position: The 1912 Agreement gives only running rights, not a line of railway; the Agency misread it and its preamble.
issues.respondent_position: The agreement confers more than running rights, including local business and interchange rights; the Agency's reading is reasonable.
issues.result_quote: CN has failed to show that the Agency’s interpretation of the nature of the rights conferred on BNSF in the 1912 Agreement was unreasonable.

issues.issue: Was it unreasonable for the Agency to exclude extrinsic evidence of BNSF's conduct?
issues.applicant_position: Evidence of BNSF's actual conduct should have been admitted to show it had not exercised local business rights.
issues.respondent_position: Extrinsic evidence was unnecessary; the Agency reasoned that an unexercised right still exists.
issues.result_quote: I do not find the Agency’s conclusion on this point to be unreasonable for the following reasons.

issues.issue: Was it unreasonable to find that BNSF had the right to interchange traffic with CN at Emerson?
issues.applicant_position: CN permitted BNSF to interchange only at Noyes under the 1977 agreement; BNSF has no right to interchange at Emerson.
issues.respondent_position: An uncontested history of interchange at Emerson, and its listing in the OPSL, show BNSF's authority.
issues.result_quote: it was not unreasonable for the Agency to find that this was sufficient to give BNSF a line of railway in Canada.

issues.issue: Did the Agency wrongly amend the 1912 Agreement and confer rights on a third party, Richardson?
issues.applicant_position: The Agency had no authority to amend a private agreement, and its order confers rights on a third party the agreement bars.
issues.respondent_position: The Agency was entitled to examine the agreement to determine the rights it conferred.
issues.result_quote: There is nothing unreasonable in this aspect of the Agency’s decision.

issues.issue: Does the BNSF line extend across the Canada-US border, so that there is a connection in Canada?
issues.applicant_position: The lines meet at the border without either crossing it; the BNSF line does not enter Canada.
issues.respondent_position: Connecting lines are physically linked over a distance exceeding a border's width; this finding is within the Agency's expertise.
issues.result_quote: I am unable to find that its characterization of the nature of connecting railway lines was unreasonable.

issues.issue: Did the Agency breach natural justice by relying on an intervener's description from another decision?
issues.applicant_position: The Agency relied on an undisclosed intervener's description from another case without giving CN a chance to respond.
issues.respondent_position: CN knew of Decision 165-R-2013 and the intervener's role; relying on the articulated principle was fair.
issues.result_quote: there was nothing unfair in the Agency’s reliance upon a principle it articulated in Decision No. 165-R-2013.

issues.issue: Did the Agency exceed its jurisdiction by applying the Act to a line beyond the Canadian border?
issues.applicant_position: Applying the Act to track outside Canada gives it impermissible extraterritorial effect.
issues.respondent_position: No extraterritorial issue arises; the Agency's jurisdiction rests on BNSF's operations in Canada.
issues.result_quote: I disagree for the reasons set out at paragraphs 19 and 20 above.

issues.issue: Does the 1912 Agreement establish a connection between the two lines, as an alternate basis for the Agency's finding?
issues.applicant_position: The 1912 Agreement creates running rights only and does not establish a connection between the lines.
issues.respondent_position: The Agreement's rights effectively permit BNSF to connect along the entire line; the Agency's reading is reasonable.
issues.result_quote: CN has not satisfied me that the Agency’s construction of the 1912 Agreement was unreasonable.

issues.issue: Was it unreasonable to order interswitching when Richardson had access to two competitive carriers?
issues.applicant_position: Interswitching presumes insufficient competition; with two carriers on one line there is perfect competition, so no order.
issues.respondent_position: Competition is not a condition in s. 127, and Parliament expressly limits remedies when it wants competition considered.
issues.result_quote: CN has not shown any error in this Court’s analysis upholding the reasonableness of the Agency’s decision.
